newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee futures end down 8.5 pct, funds sell.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee futures end down 8.5 pct, funds sell.

text.p: LIFFE robusta coffee futures tumbled to end Thursday a sharp 8.5 percent down basis July as sell-stops emerged towards the close as the contract broke the key support at $2,000.

"It's sell-stops all over the place as July broke major support at $2,000," said one trader. "There were no bids." July ended at $1,905 a tonne, down $178, after losing nearly $100 in the last 15 minutes of trading.
Profit-takers swarmed through the market to lock in profits as it turned down from last week's rally that took London to a 20-month high.
"The longs are probably tired," another said. Coffee's five-month rally since early January was almost uninterrupted and unprecedented as there had not been a frost yet in Brazil this year.
Robusta prices this year had doubled to $2,670, a 20-year-peak, on May 29 from a low of $1,203 in January.
Today's fall followed a sharp retracement in New York's arabica futures which came under pressure from speculative and trade selling.
Traders said the sell orders emerged after July broke a trendline at 250 cents to hit a low of 232 cents per lb.
Traders said Tuesday's news Colombia was opening coffee registrations for July to August period continued to provide a bearish tone.
Brazil's coffee belt was also expected to escape a damaging cold this weekend although temperatures might drop to below normal levels, weathermen said.
London showed small losses in the morning on industry buying on the dips. But roasters disappeared in the afternoon, allowing an almost a free-fall in prices.
Technically, July could struggle to hold support at $1,900. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 5424985
